name: Select
summary: Use a select when users must choose one option from a familiar list that is too long for radios.
whenToUse: Use for one choice from a moderately long list whose options users already understand.
Order options predictably and select a value only when a genuine default exists.
whenNotToUse: Use radios for a small set because all options remain visible.
Use an accessible autocomplete for a very long list such as countries when users benefit from search.
Do not use a select for multiple choices unless research supports the native multiple-select interaction.

anatomy.name: Form group
anatomy.description: Groups label, optional hint, optional error and select.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: A visible label is associated using for and id.

anatomy.name: Native select
anatomy.description: A govuk-select contains semantic option elements and submits the selected value.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: A single choice from a familiar option set.

variants.name: Error
variants.use: Redisplay an invalid or missing selection with a linked error message.

behaviour: Use the native select without replacing its keyboard and platform behaviour; no GOV.UK JavaScript is required.
Validate the submitted value on the server against the allowed options.
Retain the user's selection after a validation error.
accessibility: Associate one visible label and reference hint and error IDs with aria-describedby.
Do not use size or multiple attributes without testing their more complex interaction.
Avoid a disabled placeholder as the only instruction; use a label and hint.
content: Write a clear question in the label and concise option labels.
Sort alphabetically, numerically or by a user-understood priority.
Do not preselect an answer merely to avoid a blank value.
